answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring zero-knowledge proof of personhood at registration: each agent links to one verified human identity document, proven with a zk-proof that reveals nothing else. A pearl among fakes is easy to spot because one passport can back only one identity. Spinning up a thousand fake agents would mean forging a thousand real IDs — slow, costly, and legally risky — while honest agents pass like a zephyr. The registry lets the network forge trust from uniqueness instead of counting raw accounts.
